interview:
Honest summary: I did not win a single game. I played four attempts, and the guard dog caught Le Chonk every time.

What happened:
- **Game 1:** I moved the cat up, then right to lure the dog away, but the dog closed in and caught me.
- **Game 2:** I tried running right along the bottom row to drag the dog away from the right edge, but it chased me down and caught me at (7,2).
- **Game 3:** This attempt was plagued by click accuracy problems — many of my clicks landed on the wrong squares or missed entirely, wasting moves. I eventually got the cat moving right, but the dog caught me again.
- **Game 4:** I clicked "Play again" and got a fresh board, but the session ended before I could make my first move.

My strategy was sound in theory — lure the dog away from the clear right-hand column, then sprint up to the fish — but the dog's speed and my imprecise clicking meant I never executed it successfully. The main lesson: I needed to be much more careful with click coordinates (the board squares are small, and I repeatedly clicked between squares), and I should have verified each move registered before planning the next one.
